documents.prompt: Researchers record the average amount of sleep and the test score for each of {{n}} students but do not assign students to sleep for different amounts of time. The data show that students who sleep more tend to have higher test scores. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.label: In this study, amount of sleep is associated with test score, but the study does not establish that more sleep causes higher scores.
More sleep causes higher test scores for all students.
Higher test scores cause students to sleep more.
The study proves that sleep and test score are unrelated.

documents.prompt: Researchers randomly assign {{n}} volunteers to receive either treatment A or treatment B. The groups are otherwise treated the same, and the treatment A group has a higher average response. Which conclusion is best supported by the study design?

choices.label: The random assignment supports a cause-and-effect conclusion about the treatments for the study participants.
The result can automatically be generalized to every member of the population.
The study can show only an association because treatments were assigned at random.
No comparison between treatments is possible because volunteers participated.

documents.prompt: A researcher selects a random sample of {{n}} residents from a city's adult population and asks whether they support a proposal. Which use of the sample is most justified?

choices.label: The sample results can be used to estimate the proportion of adults in the city who support the proposal.
The survey can establish that the proposal causes residents to change their opinions.
The results apply only to the sampled residents and cannot inform the city population.
The results can be generalized to every adult in the country.

documents.prompt: To estimate how all students at a school feel about lunch choices, a survey is given only to the {{n}} students who enter the cafeteria during the first 10 minutes of lunch. What is the main limitation of this sampling method?

choices.label: The sample may not be representative of all students at the school because it is a convenience sample.
The sample is automatically representative because every surveyed student attends the school.
The sample can establish which lunch option causes greater satisfaction.
The only limitation is that the sample contains more than one student.

documents.prompt: In an experiment with {{n}} participants, the researchers randomly assign participants to a treatment group or a control group. What is the main purpose of the random assignment?

choices.label: To reduce systematic differences between the groups so treatment effects can be compared more fairly.
To make the participants a random sample of the entire population.
To guarantee that both groups will have exactly the same outcomes.
To increase the population size represented by the experiment.

documents.prompt: Researchers randomly sample {{n}} eligible adults from a population and then randomly assign the sampled adults to treatment or control groups. A meaningful difference in outcomes is observed. Which conclusion is best supported by this design?

choices.label: The random assignment supports a causal conclusion, and the random sampling supports generalizing the result to the population represented by the sample.
The design supports generalization but not a causal conclusion.
The design supports a causal conclusion but never permits population generalization.
The design supports neither causation nor generalization because both steps were random.

documents.prompt: {{n}} volunteers respond to an advertisement for a study. The volunteers are then randomly assigned to treatment and control groups. Which statement best describes what the study design supports?

choices.label: Random assignment supports a causal comparison for the participants, but the volunteer sample limits how broadly the result can be generalized.
The volunteer sample makes the study a random sample of the population.
The study can be generalized broadly but cannot support a causal conclusion.
Random assignment removes the need for a comparison group.

documents.prompt: A random sample of {{n}} adults is selected from a population. Researchers record each person's weekly exercise time and resting heart rate without assigning an exercise amount. The variables are associated in the sample. Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.label: The association can be used to describe the population represented by the random sample, but the observational design does not establish that exercise causes the difference in heart rate.
The random sample proves that additional exercise causes a lower resting heart rate.
Because the study is observational, the sample cannot provide any information about the population.
Random sampling and random assignment are the same feature of a study design.
